Today you turn your `ch2-practice` project into a small website for your advisor, who wants to see the Nebraska yield results with their code and checks. The AI writes the configuration and the pages; you decide what the site holds, and you judge it by using it.

**Rules:**

A. Write the site map **before** you ask the AI.

B. Keep the requests you actually sent in this file, with the blanks filled in.

C. You judge the site by rendering it and clicking through it, starting from the home page.

# Task 3: Ask the AI for the site

**My request to the AI.** Fill in every `<...>` from Tasks 1 and 2, then send it:

```text
Turn my project folder ch2-practice into a Quarto website. The visitor
is my advisor, who wants to see the latest results with their code and
checks. Pages, in this order in the menu at the top:
<numbered list: page name, file name, what it shows>
Leave out <files or folders that must not become pages>. Every page
reads the data it needs itself, from data/2-1-nebraska-yield.csv. On
the page that reads the data, check the number of rows (I expect
<number>) and the years covered (I expect <first year> to <last year>).

Put the code in my Quarto document <path of the data page's .qmd>,
under the heading "<heading>", as R code chunks. Above each chunk,
write one plain-English sentence saying what it does and why. Build
every path with here::here(); no setwd(), no absolute paths. Print each
check on its own line as "name of check: expected X, got Y". Render
the document to HTML.
```
